quotes.name: Omar Amici
quotes.quote: To be honest, the changes in Uptown have me feeling a bit uneasy. The streets are busier than ever, and it seems like every other place is a for-rent sign these days. I've lived here long enough to see the neighborhood transform, but this feels different. It's like the neighborhood is shifting away from the people who've been here all along. I put on my good suit for Sunday service because some traditions still matter, but walking around, I see more strangers than familiar faces. It's hard not to wonder if this is still my neighborhood or if I'm just a ghost walking through someone else's plans.

quotes.name: Bobby Chen-Ramirez
quotes.quote: To be honest, Omar Amici's perspective on neighborhood change isn't something I've directly heard, but I can relate to the feeling. Seeing a moving van block the bike lane as another new resident unboxes in Jack London makes me wonder if we're losing the neighborhood I know. I've been so focused on getting our health center up and running, making sure Mrs. Okafor can get her blood pressure checked without taking two buses. But when I see the crane's shadows stretching long over our building, it's a reminder that change is all around us. I'm not sure what Omar Amici thinks, but I know I've got to keep my eyes on the prize - making sure our community benefits from all this development.

quotes.name: Elena Soria Dominguez
quotes.quote: I've compared notes with Dmitri Soto over coffee, and he's been feeling the same pinch I have about the changes around here. People like Omar Amici are probably wondering if their neighborhood is still theirs or if it's just becoming someone else's plan. I've seen it in my own life - when I caught my reflection in a shop window, I stood a little straighter, but it's hard not to feel like you're just trying to fit into someone else's picture sometimes.

quotes.name: Keisha Ramos
quotes.quote: To be honest, Omar Amici's perspective on neighborhood change isn't directly something I've been thinking about, but what does resonate with me is the feeling of being accountable to the community. I've been working hard on the Baylight Redevelopment, and it's not just about meeting deadlines or getting the job done; it's about making sure what we build actually works for the people who live here. Like, we're waiting on those soil test results for the C115 review, and that's a big deal because it affects the whole remediation calendar. It's not just about checking boxes; it's about proving that what we've done makes a real difference. I wish I could say that Omar Amici's perspective is something I've been directly grappling with, but the accountability part is something that keeps me up at night.

interviews.name: Keisha Ramos
interviews.quote: To be honest, Omar Amici's perspective on neighborhood change isn't directly something I've been thinking about, but what does resonate with me is the feeling of being accountable to the community. I've been working hard on the Baylight Redevelopment, and it's not just about meeting deadlines or getting the job done; it's about making sure what we build actually works for the people who live here. Like, we're waiting on those soil test results for the C115 review, and that's a big deal because it affects the whole remediation calendar. It's not just about checking boxes; it's about proving that what we've done makes a real difference. I wish I could say that Omar Amici's perspective is something I've been directly grappling with, but the accountability part is something that keeps me up at night.
